# 15. Enterprise Autonomous Operating Model Architecture Framework

## 15.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Autonomous Operating Model Architecture Framework establishes the canonical methodology for designing the operating model required to translate Enterprise Strategy, Enterprise Architecture, governance, autonomous capabilities, intelligent decision-making, human expertise, technology, information, and operational execution into a coherent enterprise operating system.

The operating model shall define how the enterprise creates, delivers, governs, measures, protects, and continuously improves Enterprise Value.

The Autonomous Enterprise shall not be understood merely as an organization with automated processes.

It shall be understood as:

```text
Enterprise Purpose

↓

Enterprise Strategy

↓

Enterprise Capabilities

↓

Operating Model

↓

People + AI + Agents + Automation

↓

Enterprise Processes

↓

Decisions

↓

Execution

↓

Enterprise Outcomes

↓

Enterprise Value

↓

Continuous Learning
```

Enterprise Architects shall ensure that the operating model remains aligned with governance authority, enterprise risk appetite, strategic intent, organizational capability, technology architecture, information architecture, and measurable enterprise outcomes.

---

## 15.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Autonomous Operating Model Architecture Framework shall:

- establish a coherent autonomous operating model
- connect strategy with operational execution
- integrate people, AI, agents, automation, and technology
- define operating responsibilities
- establish decision and execution relationships
- strengthen operational governance
- improve enterprise agility
- improve enterprise resilience
- enable continuous optimization
- support controlled enterprise autonomy
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 15.3 Operating Model Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Enterprise Purpose

↓

Enterprise Strategy

↓

Strategic Capabilities

↓

Value Streams

↓

Operating Model

↓

Organizational Model

↓

Decision Model

↓

Process Model

↓

Information Model

↓

Technology & AI Services

↓

Autonomous Capabilities

↓

Operational Execution

↓

Enterprise Outcomes
```

The operating model shall provide the connection between what the enterprise intends to achieve and how the enterprise actually performs.

---

## 15.4 Operating Model Domains

The Autonomous Operating Model shall govern:

### Strategic Operating Model

Defines:

- enterprise priorities
- strategic capabilities
- strategic decision rights
- strategic resource allocation
- transformation priorities
- enterprise performance

---

### Organizational Operating Model

Defines:

- organizational structures
- roles
- responsibilities
- accountability
- capability ownership
- collaboration models
- human–AI responsibilities

---

### Capability Operating Model

Defines:

- enterprise capabilities
- capability ownership
- capability maturity
- capability dependencies
- capability performance
- capability evolution

---

### Value Stream Operating Model

Defines:

- value streams
- value stages
- stakeholders
- value outcomes
- value dependencies
- value performance
- value improvement

---

### Process Operating Model

Defines:

- enterprise processes
- workflows
- decision points
- process ownership
- process controls
- process automation
- process performance

---

### Information Operating Model

Defines:

- information flows
- information ownership
- knowledge access
- information quality
- semantic relationships
- information governance
- information lifecycle

---

### Technology Operating Model

Defines:

- technology platforms
- applications
- infrastructure
- integration
- APIs
- cloud services
- AI services
- agent platforms

---

### Governance Operating Model

Defines:

- governance structures
- policies
- authority
- decision rights
- controls
- assurance
- escalation

---

## 15.5 Autonomous Operating Model

The Autonomous Operating Model shall integrate:

```text
Human Expertise

+

Artificial Intelligence

+

Intelligent Agents

+

Automation

+

Digital Services

+

Enterprise Data

+

Enterprise Knowledge

+

Enterprise Processes

+

Governance

=

Integrated Autonomous Operating Capability
```

The objective shall not be to replace human responsibility indiscriminately.

The objective shall be to allocate work, decisions, and execution to the most appropriate combination of:

- humans;
- AI;
- agents;
- automation;
- enterprise services.

Allocation shall be determined by:

- risk;
- complexity;
- accountability;
- reversibility;
- required judgment;
- speed;
- scale;
- cost;
- enterprise value.

---

## 15.6 Operating Responsibility Model

Every material enterprise activity shall have explicitly defined responsibility.

Responsibility shall identify:

- accountable owner
- responsible capability
- executing party
- decision authority
- supporting services
- AI involvement
- agent involvement
- human oversight
- escalation authority

The responsibility relationship shall be:

```text
Accountability

↓

Authority

↓

Responsibility

↓

Execution

↓

Evidence

↓

Outcome
```

No material autonomous capability shall operate without an identifiable accountable owner.

---

## 15.7 Autonomous Work Allocation

The enterprise shall determine whether an activity should be:

### Human-Executed

Where judgment, accountability, ethical reasoning, or contextual interpretation requires direct human participation.

### Human-Assisted

Where AI or automation increases human capability while the human retains decision authority.

### AI-Assisted

Where AI provides analysis, recommendations, prediction, classification, or decision support.

### Agent-Executed

Where an authorized agent performs defined activities within explicit boundaries.

### Fully Automated

Where deterministic or highly controlled execution can occur without continuous human intervention.

### Autonomous

Where an intelligent capability can independently sense, decide, act, observe, and adapt within approved governance boundaries.

The selected operating mode shall remain proportional to enterprise risk and consequence.

---

## 15.8 Decision and Execution Architecture

The operating model shall distinguish between:

- sensing
- analysis
- recommendation
- authorization
- decision
- execution
- monitoring
- intervention
- learning

The architecture shall support:

```text
Sense

↓

Understand

↓

Evaluate

↓

Recommend

↓

Authorize

↓

Decide

↓

Act

↓

Observe

↓

Learn
```

Not every activity requires all stages to be performed by the same actor.

The operating model shall explicitly identify which participant performs each stage.

---

## 15.9 Operating Model Performance

The Enterprise Autonomous Operating Model Architecture Framework shall evaluate:

- operating model maturity
- capability performance
- process performance
- decision effectiveness
- autonomy effectiveness
- human–AI collaboration
- operational resilience
- resource utilization
- cost efficiency
- enterprise agility
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance indicators shall continuously strengthen the enterprise operating model.

---

# 16. Enterprise Autonomous Operating Governance Integration Framework

## 16.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Autonomous Operating Governance Integration Framework establishes the canonical methodology for integrating governance directly into the Autonomous Enterprise operating model.

Governance shall not operate as a separate layer disconnected from execution.

Instead:

```text
Governance

+

Operating Model

+

Architecture

+

Risk

+

Security

+

Information

+

Decision Intelligence

+

Execution

=

Integrated Enterprise Operating System
```

The framework ensures that enterprise policies, authority, risk controls, human oversight, assurance, and governance intelligence are continuously connected to operational execution.

---

## 16.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Autonomous Operating Governance Integration Framework shall:

- integrate governance with operational execution
- connect policy with enterprise processes
- connect authority with decisions
- connect risk with operating activities
- connect controls with execution
- connect evidence with assurance
- connect outcomes with governance learning
- strengthen operational accountability
- improve governance responsiveness
- support continuously governed autonomy
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 16.3 Integrated Operating Governance Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Enterprise Strategy

↓

Governance Policy

↓

Authority

↓

Operating Model

↓

Capability

↓

Process

↓

Decision

↓

Autonomous Execution

↓

Continuous Observation

↓

Risk & Control Assessment

↓

Governance Evidence

↓

Assurance

↓

Governance Intelligence

↓

Learning

↓

Operating Model Evolution
```

Governance shall remain embedded within the operating model rather than operating only through periodic reviews.

---

## 16.4 Governance-to-Execution Traceability

Every material governed activity shall support traceability between:

- strategic objective
- policy
- authority
- capability
- process
- decision
- action
- control
- outcome
- evidence

The traceability chain shall be:

```text
Objective

↓

Policy

↓

Authority

↓

Capability

↓

Process

↓

Decision

↓

Action

↓

Control

↓

Outcome

↓

Evidence
```

This traceability shall support operational accountability and continuous assurance.

---

## 16.5 Embedded Policy Architecture

Policies shall be translated into operationally meaningful requirements.

Policy implementation may include:

- enterprise policies
- standards
- rules
- decision constraints
- Policy-as-Code
- workflow controls
- access controls
- transaction controls
- AI controls
- agent controls

Policies shall remain linked to:

- policy owner
- policy purpose
- authority
- applicable capability
- applicable process
- applicable risk
- control implementation
- evidence

---

## 16.6 Embedded Authority Architecture

Authority shall be integrated directly into operating execution.

Authority shall define:

- who or what may act
- what may be done
- under which conditions
- within which boundaries
- with which resources
- at which risk level
- for which duration
- subject to which escalation conditions

Autonomous agents and AI-enabled services shall not infer authority solely from technical access.

Technical access and governance authority shall remain separate architectural concepts.

---

## 16.7 Embedded Risk Architecture

Operational activities shall continuously consider relevant risk.

Risk-aware execution shall evaluate:

- current risk
- risk appetite
- risk threshold
- control status
- environmental conditions
- security conditions
- information quality
- operational dependencies
- decision confidence

The operating model shall support dynamic adjustment of:

- autonomy;
- controls;
- monitoring;
- escalation;
- human oversight.

---

## 16.8 Embedded Human Oversight

Human oversight shall be embedded within operational execution where required.

The operating model shall support:

- approval
- supervision
- intervention
- override
- escalation
- suspension
- authority revocation
- emergency response

Human intervention shall be available at the point where the relevant decision or action occurs.

Oversight shall therefore not depend exclusively on retrospective governance review.

---

## 16.9 Embedded Assurance

Assurance shall operate continuously where appropriate.

The operating model shall generate evidence concerning:

- decisions
- actions
- policies
- authorities
- controls
- risks
- exceptions
- interventions
- outcomes

Evidence shall support:

- operational assurance
- governance assurance
- security assurance
- compliance
- audit
- architecture review
- continuous learning

---

Governance shall be capable of responding to operational events.

Material governance events may include:

- policy violation
- authority violation
- risk threshold breach
- control failure
- security event
- abnormal agent behavior
- AI model degradation
- process deviation
- operational failure
- material business impact

The governance response shall follow:

```text
Event

↓

Detection

↓

Classification

↓

Context

↓

Risk Assessment

↓

Authority Check

↓

Governance Response

↓

Execution

↓

Verification

↓

Evidence

↓

Learning
```

---

## 16.11 Operating Governance Escalation

Escalation shall be proportional to:

- impact
- urgency
- uncertainty
- reversibility
- risk
- authority
- regulatory significance

Escalation shall normally proceed through:

```text
Operational Capability

↓

Process Owner

↓

Capability Owner

↓

Governance Authority

↓

Executive Authority

↓

Enterprise Leadership
```

Critical events may bypass normal escalation paths when emergency governance conditions require immediate intervention.

---

## 16.12 Operating Governance Feedback

Operational outcomes shall continuously feed governance.

The feedback relationship is:

```text

↓

Performance

↓

Risk

↓

↓
```

Governance shall therefore remain a learning system rather than a static approval mechanism.

## 16.13 Operating Governance Performance

The Enterprise Autonomous Operating Governance Integration Framework shall evaluate:

- governance integration
- policy effectiveness

- control effectiveness
- escalation effectiveness

- evidence completeness

The Enterprise Autonomous Operating Model Architecture Framework and the Enterprise Autonomous Operating Governance Integration Framework shall remain:

- purpose-driven
- capability-centric
- governance-controlled
- policy-based
- authority-aware
- human-accountable
- risk-proportional

# EA-IMETA76

# Enterprise Architecture Autonomous Enterprise Governance & Operating Model

## Document Version 1.0

### Part 2 of 6

#### Section 2 of 8

---

# 17. Enterprise Autonomous Capability Operating Model Framework

## 17.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Autonomous Capability Operating Model Framework establishes the canonical methodology for designing, governing, operating, measuring, and continuously evolving enterprise capabilities that incorporate Artificial Intelligence, intelligent agents, automation, digital services, human expertise, information, and technology.

Enterprise capabilities shall represent what the enterprise must be able to do in order to achieve its strategic objectives.

Within an Autonomous Enterprise, capabilities increasingly become intelligent, adaptive, connected, and partially or fully executable through digital and autonomous mechanisms.

Enterprise Architects shall therefore ensure that every autonomous capability remains connected to:

- enterprise purpose
- strategic objectives
- value streams
- operating responsibilities
- governance
- authority
- risk
- information
- technology
- human expertise
- enterprise outcomes

The objective is not simply to automate capabilities.

The objective is:

> **To create governed enterprise capabilities that can sense, decide, act, learn, and evolve within approved architectural and governance boundaries.**

---

## 17.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Autonomous Capability Operating Model Framework shall:

- establish a common autonomous capability model
- connect capabilities with enterprise strategy
- define capability ownership
- establish capability operating responsibilities
- integrate humans, AI, agents, and automation
- strengthen capability governance
- improve capability observability
- improve capability resilience
- enable capability evolution
- support controlled autonomy
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 17.3 Autonomous Capability Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Enterprise Purpose

↓

Strategic Objective

↓

Enterprise Capability

↓

Capability Outcome

↓

Capability Operating Model

↓

People + AI + Agents + Automation

↓

Processes + Information + Technology

↓

Capability Execution

↓

Capability Performance

↓

Capability Learning

↓

Capability Evolution
```

Every material capability shall have a defined purpose, owner, outcome, operating model, governance model, performance model, and evolution path.

---

## 17.4 Capability Domains

Autonomous enterprise capabilities shall be classified according to their primary purpose.

### Strategic Capabilities

Capabilities directly supporting enterprise strategy, transformation, investment, strategic decision-making, and long-term enterprise development.

---

### Customer Capabilities

Capabilities supporting customer acquisition, customer service, customer experience, customer intelligence, customer engagement, and relationship management.

---

### Commercial Capabilities

Capabilities supporting sales, pricing, contracting, revenue management, market management, and commercial optimization.

---

### Operational Capabilities

Capabilities supporting service delivery, production, logistics, supply chain, resource management, and operational execution.

---

### Financial Capabilities

Capabilities supporting financial management, accounting, forecasting, treasury, budgeting, investment management, and financial control.

---

### Information Capabilities

Capabilities supporting data management, information management, knowledge management, analytics, intelligence, and enterprise information governance.

---

### Technology Capabilities

Capabilities supporting technology platforms, applications, infrastructure, integration, cloud services, AI services, and digital platforms.

---

### Governance Capabilities

Capabilities supporting policy management, authority management, risk management, compliance, assurance, audit, and governance intelligence.

---

### Security Capabilities

Capabilities supporting identity, cybersecurity, Zero Trust, threat management, resilience, incident response, and security assurance.

---

### Organizational Capabilities

Capabilities supporting people, workforce management, organizational development, collaboration, knowledge transfer, and enterprise learning.

---

## 17.5 Capability Ownership

Every material enterprise capability shall have explicit ownership.

Capability ownership shall identify:

- accountable owner
- capability manager
- operating owner
- decision authority
- supporting capabilities
- technology ownership
- information ownership
- AI ownership where applicable
- agent ownership where applicable
- assurance ownership

Capability ownership shall remain traceable throughout the capability lifecycle.

No material autonomous capability shall operate without identifiable accountability.

---

## 17.6 Capability Operating Modes

Enterprise capabilities may operate through different modes.

### Human-Centric Capability

Humans perform the primary activities while technology provides supporting services.

### Human-Augmented Capability

Humans remain responsible while AI, automation, and digital services significantly increase capability performance.

### AI-Assisted Capability

AI performs analysis, prediction, classification, recommendation, or decision support while authorized humans retain decision authority.

### Agent-Assisted Capability

Intelligent agents perform defined activities under human or governance supervision.

### Agent-Executed Capability

Authorized agents execute defined activities within explicit authority and operating boundaries.

### Autonomous Capability

The capability can independently sense, evaluate, decide, act, observe, and adapt within approved governance constraints.

The operating mode shall be selected according to:

- risk
- consequence
- complexity
- reversibility
- required judgment
- accountability
- speed
- scale
- enterprise value

---

## 17.7 Capability Composition

Autonomous capabilities shall be composed from reusable enterprise building blocks.

A capability may include:

- people
- processes
- information
- knowledge
- applications
- AI models
- agents
- automation
- technology platforms
- controls
- governance services
- security services
- resilience mechanisms

The capability composition model is:

```text
Capability

├── People

├── Process

├── Information

├── Knowledge

├── Applications

├── AI

├── Agents

├── Automation

├── Technology

├── Governance

├── Security

└── Resilience
```

Enterprise Architects shall seek modular capability composition to support reuse, scalability, resilience, and controlled evolution.

---

## 17.8 Capability Dependencies

Every material capability shall identify dependencies on:

- other capabilities
- value streams
- processes
- information
- applications
- technology platforms
- AI models
- autonomous agents
- external services
- suppliers
- governance services
- security services

Dependencies shall be assessed for:

- criticality
- resilience
- concentration
- failure propagation
- recovery requirements
- strategic significance

---

## 17.9 Capability Decision Model

Autonomous capabilities shall explicitly define the decisions they are permitted to make.

Decision definitions shall include:

- decision type
- decision owner
- decision authority
- decision inputs
- decision criteria
- policy constraints
- risk thresholds
- confidence requirements
- escalation conditions
- human oversight
- evidence requirements

The decision model is:

```text
Context

↓

Information

↓

Policy

↓

Risk

↓

Authority

↓

Decision

↓

Action

↓

Outcome

↓

Evidence
```

No autonomous capability shall make material decisions outside its approved decision authority.

---

## 17.10 Capability Performance

Capability performance shall be evaluated according to:

- outcome achievement
- service quality
- decision quality
- process efficiency
- autonomy effectiveness
- reliability
- resilience
- resource utilization
- cost
- risk
- stakeholder experience
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance measurement shall include both operational performance and governance performance.

---

## 17.11 Capability Observability

Material autonomous capabilities shall remain observable.

Observability shall include, where appropriate:

- capability state
- operating state
- decision state
- AI model state
- agent state
- information state
- dependency state
- security state
- risk state
- control state
- outcome state

Observability shall support operational management, assurance, incident investigation, and continuous learning.

---

## 17.12 Capability Resilience

Autonomous capabilities shall be designed for resilience.

Resilience shall include:

- redundancy
- graceful degradation
- failure containment
- recovery
- fallback operating modes
- human intervention
- capability isolation
- dependency management
- continuity
- recovery testing

Critical capabilities shall have explicitly defined recovery objectives and governance requirements.

---

## 17.13 Capability Evolution

Capabilities shall continuously evolve in response to:

- strategic change
- customer change
- operational experience
- technology change
- AI evolution
- agent evolution
- regulatory change
- risk change
- security threats
- performance results
- enterprise learning

Capability evolution shall remain governed.

Material changes shall trigger appropriate:

- architecture review
- risk assessment
- policy review
- authority review
- security review
- assurance
- deployment governance

---

## 17.14 Capability Lifecycle

The autonomous capability lifecycle shall be:

```text
Capability Identification

↓

Capability Design

↓

Capability Assessment

↓

Capability Authorization

↓

Capability Deployment

↓

Capability Operation

↓

Capability Monitoring

↓

Capability Assurance

↓

Capability Optimization

↓

Capability Evolution

↓

Capability Retirement
```

The lifecycle shall remain connected to enterprise strategy and enterprise architecture.

---

## 17.15 Capability Performance and Maturity

The Enterprise Autonomous Capability Operating Model Framework shall evaluate:

- capability maturity
- autonomy maturity
- capability effectiveness
- capability resilience
- capability observability
- capability governance
- capability risk
- capability innovation
- capability scalability
- capability adaptability
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance indicators shall continuously strengthen enterprise capability management.

---

# 18. Enterprise Autonomous Value Stream Operating Framework

## 18.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Autonomous Value Stream Operating Framework establishes the canonical methodology for designing, operating, governing, measuring, and continuously improving value streams in an Autonomous Enterprise.

Value streams represent how enterprise capabilities combine to create outcomes for customers, stakeholders, partners, owners, employees, and other relevant beneficiaries.

Within an Autonomous Enterprise, value streams increasingly operate through coordinated combinations of:

- people
- AI
- intelligent agents
- automation
- digital services
- information
- enterprise capabilities

Enterprise Architects shall therefore ensure that value stream design remains connected to enterprise strategy, customer outcomes, capability architecture, governance, operating models, and measurable Enterprise Value.

---

## 18.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Autonomous Value Stream Operating Framework shall:

- establish a common autonomous value stream model
- connect strategy with value delivery
- improve value stream visibility
- integrate capabilities across value stages
- identify opportunities for autonomy
- strengthen value governance
- improve customer and stakeholder outcomes
- improve value stream resilience
- enable continuous optimization
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 18.3 Value Stream Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Stakeholder Need

↓

Value Proposition

↓

Value Stream

↓

Value Stage

↓

Capability

↓

Process

↓

Decision

↓

Execution

↓

Outcome

↓

Stakeholder Value

↓

Learning

↓

Value Stream Evolution
```

Each value stream shall have a defined stakeholder, value proposition, outcome, owner, capabilities, dependencies, governance model, and performance model.

---

## 18.4 Value Stream Domains

Value streams may include:

### Customer Value Streams

Activities transforming customer needs into customer outcomes.

---

### Product and Service Value Streams

Activities transforming ideas, requirements, resources, and capabilities into products and services.

---

### Commercial Value Streams

Activities transforming market opportunities into contracts, revenue, and commercial relationships.

---

### Operational Value Streams

Activities transforming resources and operational inputs into reliable products, services, or outcomes.

---

### Financial Value Streams

Activities transforming financial information, resources, and decisions into financial control, liquidity, investment, and enterprise value.

---

### Innovation Value Streams

Activities transforming ideas, research, experimentation, and knowledge into new capabilities, products, services, or operating models.

---

### Governance Value Streams

Activities transforming governance requirements and enterprise conditions into controlled decisions, approvals, assurance, and enterprise protection.

---

### Enterprise Transformation Value Streams

Activities transforming strategic intent into new capabilities, architecture, operating models, technologies, and enterprise outcomes.

---

## 18.5 Value Stage Architecture

Each value stream shall be decomposed into meaningful value stages.

A generic autonomous value stage may follow:

```text
Sense Need

↓

Understand Context

↓

Evaluate Options

↓

Decide

↓

Execute

↓

Deliver Outcome

↓

Measure Value

↓

Learn

↓

Improve
```

Not every value stream requires the same sequence.

Enterprise Architects shall design stages according to the actual value creation logic of the enterprise.

---

## 18.6 Autonomous Value Stream Design

Each value stream shall identify where work can be:

- human-executed
- human-assisted
- AI-assisted
- agent-assisted
- agent-executed
- automated
- autonomous

The allocation shall consider:

- customer impact
- enterprise risk
- decision complexity
- accountability
- reversibility
- required human judgment
- speed
- scale
- cost
- enterprise value

Autonomy shall be applied to increase value rather than merely to increase automation.

---

## 18.7 Value Stream Governance

Each material value stream shall define:

- value stream owner
- stakeholder
- value objective
- accountable authority
- participating capabilities
- governance requirements
- policies
- controls
- risks
- performance measures
- escalation mechanisms
- assurance requirements

Governance shall remain integrated across the complete value stream.

---

## 18.8 Value Stream Dependencies

Value stream dependencies shall include:

- capabilities
- processes
- information
- applications
- AI models
- agents
- technology
- suppliers
- partners
- external services
- governance services

Dependencies shall be assessed for:

- criticality
- resilience
- concentration
- failure propagation
- recovery
- strategic importance

---

## 18.9 Value Stream Performance

Value stream performance shall measure:

- stakeholder outcome
- customer experience
- value realization
- cycle time
- quality
- reliability
- cost
- productivity
- resilience
- risk
- autonomy effectiveness
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance shall be measured across the complete value stream rather than only at individual process stages.

---

## 18.10 Value Stream Observability

Autonomous value streams shall remain observable.

Observability shall provide visibility into:

- value stage status
- capability performance
- decision points
- process conditions
- AI performance
- agent performance
- dependency conditions
- risk
- controls
- stakeholder outcomes

This observability shall support real-time operational management and continuous value optimization.

---

## 18.11 Value Stream Resilience

Critical value streams shall be designed for resilience.

Resilience shall include:

- alternative capabilities
- alternative processes
- redundancy
- dependency diversity
- fallback execution
- human intervention
- service isolation
- recovery
- continuity
- resilience testing

The enterprise shall identify value streams where failure would materially affect enterprise purpose or strategic objectives.

---

## 18.12 Value Stream Optimization

Value streams shall be continuously optimized using:

- performance data
- customer feedback
- operational intelligence
- governance evidence
- risk information
- AI insights
- agent insights
- architecture intelligence
- financial outcomes

Optimization may involve:

- removing unnecessary activities
- improving decisions
- reallocating work
- increasing automation
- increasing autonomy
- strengthening controls
- changing capabilities
- changing technology
- redesigning value stages

Optimization shall remain bounded by governance and enterprise strategy.

---

## 18.13 Value Stream Evolution

Value streams shall evolve in response to:

- changing stakeholder needs
- market conditions
- enterprise strategy
- technology
- AI
- agent capabilities
- regulation
- risk
- security
- enterprise performance

Material changes shall trigger appropriate architecture, governance, risk, security, and assurance activities.

---

## 18.14 Value Stream Lifecycle

The value stream lifecycle shall be:

```text
Value Stream Identification

↓

Value Definition

↓

Value Stream Design

↓

Capability Mapping

↓

Operating Model Design

↓

Governance Design

↓

Implementation

↓

Operational Monitoring

↓

Value Measurement

↓

Optimization

↓

Evolution

↓

Retirement or Replacement
```

Value stream lifecycle management shall remain integrated with enterprise architecture.

---

## 18.15 Value Stream Performance and Maturity

The Enterprise Autonomous Value Stream Operating Framework shall evaluate:

- value stream maturity
- stakeholder value
- value realization
- autonomy maturity
- capability effectiveness
- operational efficiency
- resilience
- governance effectiveness
- innovation
- adaptability
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance indicators shall continuously strengthen the enterprise value system.

---

## Implementation Characteristics

The Enterprise Autonomous Capability Operating Model Framework and the Enterprise Autonomous Value Stream Operating Framework shall remain:

- purpose-driven
- capability-centric
- value-oriented
- governance-controlled
- policy-based
- authority-aware
- human-accountable
- risk-proportional
- intelligence-enabled
- evidence-driven
- observable
- resilient
- measurable
- continuously evolving

These implementation characteristics establish the capability and value-stream foundation of the Autonomous Enterprise, enabling enterprise capabilities and value streams to operate as governed, intelligent, resilient, measurable, and continuously improving systems.

---

**End of Part 2 – Section 2 of 8**

# 19. Enterprise Autonomous Process Operating Model Framework

## 19.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Autonomous Process Operating Model Framework establishes the canonical methodology for designing, governing, operating, measuring, automating, and continuously evolving enterprise processes within an Autonomous Enterprise.

Enterprise processes translate capabilities and value streams into repeatable operational activity.

Within an Autonomous Enterprise, processes may increasingly sense conditions, evaluate context, make decisions, initiate actions, coordinate resources, monitor outcomes, and adapt their execution through Artificial Intelligence, intelligent agents, automation, digital services, and human expertise.

Enterprise Architects shall therefore ensure that process design remains connected to:

- enterprise strategy
- enterprise capabilities
- value streams
- governance
- policies
- authority
- information
- technology
- AI
- agents
- security
- risk
- enterprise outcomes

The objective is not simply to automate existing processes.

The objective is:

> **To engineer governed, intelligent, resilient, measurable, and continuously improving enterprise processes.**

---

## 19.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Autonomous Process Operating Model Framework shall:

- establish a common autonomous process model
- connect processes with capabilities and value streams
- define process ownership
- integrate humans, AI, agents, and automation
- improve process performance
- strengthen process governance
- improve process observability
- strengthen process resilience
- enable continuous process optimization
- support controlled autonomy
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 19.3 Autonomous Process Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Enterprise Objective

↓

Value Stream

↓

Capability

↓

Process

↓

Process Stage

↓

Decision Point

↓

Human + AI + Agent + Automation

↓

Execution

↓

Observation

↓

Outcome

↓

Learning

↓

Process Evolution
```

Every material enterprise process shall have a defined purpose, owner, inputs, outputs, decision points, controls, dependencies, performance measures, and evolution path.

---

## 19.4 Process Domains

Autonomous enterprise processes shall be classified according to their primary purpose.

### Strategic Processes

Processes supporting:

- strategy development
- strategic planning
- investment
- transformation
- enterprise performance
- executive decision-making

---

### Customer Processes

Processes supporting:

- customer acquisition
- customer onboarding
- customer service
- customer engagement
- customer support
- customer retention

---

### Commercial Processes

Processes supporting:

- sales
- pricing
- contracting
- order management
- revenue management
- commercial analysis

---

### Operational Processes

Processes supporting:

- service delivery
- production
- logistics
- supply chain
- scheduling
- resource management
- operational control

---

### Financial Processes

Processes supporting:

- accounting
- budgeting
- forecasting
- payments
- treasury
- financial reporting
- financial control

---

### Information Processes

Processes supporting:

- data acquisition
- data management
- information quality
- knowledge management
- analytics
- information governance

---

### Technology Processes

Processes supporting:

- application management
- infrastructure management
- deployment
- integration
- technology lifecycle
- platform operations

---

### Governance Processes

Processes supporting:

- policy management
- authority management
- risk management
- compliance
- assurance
- audit
- governance reporting

---

### Security Processes

Processes supporting:

- identity management
- access management
- threat detection
- incident response
- vulnerability management
- cyber resilience

---

## 19.5 Process Ownership

Every material enterprise process shall have explicit ownership.

Process ownership shall identify:

- accountable process owner
- process manager
- capability owner
- value stream owner
- decision authority
- execution responsibility
- control owner
- information owner
- AI responsibility where applicable
- agent responsibility where applicable
- assurance responsibility

Process ownership shall remain traceable throughout the process lifecycle.

---

## 19.6 Process Operating Modes

Enterprise processes may operate through several modes.

### Human-Executed Process

Humans perform the primary activities and decisions.

### Human-Assisted Process

Technology and AI augment human execution while humans retain responsibility.

### AI-Assisted Process

AI performs analysis, classification, prediction, recommendation, or decision support.

### Agent-Assisted Process

Intelligent agents perform defined activities under human or governance supervision.

### Agent-Executed Process

Authorized agents execute defined process activities within explicit boundaries.

### Automated Process

Deterministic or highly controlled process activities execute automatically.

### Autonomous Process

The process can independently sense, decide, act, monitor, and adapt within approved governance constraints.

The selected operating mode shall be proportional to:

- risk
- complexity
- consequence
- reversibility
- required judgment
- accountability
- speed
- scale
- enterprise value

---

## 19.7 Process Decomposition

Processes shall be decomposed into meaningful stages.

A generic autonomous process may consist of:

```text
Trigger

↓

Context Acquisition

↓

Information Validation

↓

Analysis

↓

Decision

↓

Authorization

↓

Execution

↓

Verification

↓

Outcome

↓

Evidence

↓

Learning
```

Not every process requires every stage to be autonomous.

Enterprise Architects shall explicitly identify the actor responsible for each stage.

---

## 19.8 Process Decision Points

Decision points shall identify:

- decision purpose
- decision owner
- authority
- inputs
- policies
- risk conditions
- decision criteria
- confidence requirements
- escalation conditions
- human oversight
- evidence requirements

Decision points shall remain observable and traceable.

Material decisions shall not be executed outside approved authority.

---

## 19.9 Process Controls

Process controls shall include:

### Preventive Controls

Controls preventing unauthorized or unsafe process execution.

### Detective Controls

Controls identifying deviations, anomalies, or policy violations.

### Corrective Controls

Controls restoring the process to an approved state.

### Compensating Controls

Controls reducing risk where primary controls are insufficient.

### Adaptive Controls

Controls responding to validated changes in process conditions.

The control model is:

```text
Prevent

↓

Detect

↓

Correct

↓

Compensate

↓

Adapt
```

---

## 19.10 Process Observability

Material autonomous processes shall remain observable.

Observability shall provide visibility into:

- process state
- stage state
- decision state
- AI state
- agent state
- information state
- dependency state
- control state
- risk state
- outcome state

Observability shall support:

- operational management
- governance
- assurance
- incident investigation
- continuous improvement

---

## 19.11 Process Resilience

Critical processes shall be designed for resilience.

Resilience shall include:

- alternative execution paths
- redundancy
- graceful degradation
- failure containment
- fallback procedures
- human intervention
- dependency management
- recovery
- continuity
- resilience testing

Critical processes shall have explicitly defined recovery requirements.

---

## 19.12 Process Exception Management

Every material autonomous process shall define exception handling.

Exceptions may include:

- insufficient information
- policy conflict
- authority limitation
- unavailable dependency
- unexpected process condition
- abnormal AI behavior
- abnormal agent behavior
- security event
- excessive risk
- operational failure

The exception lifecycle shall be:

```text
Exception Detection

↓

Classification

↓

Risk Assessment

↓

Escalation

↓

Decision

↓

Controlled Response

↓

Verification

↓

Closure

↓

Learning
```

---

## 19.13 Process Performance

Process performance shall be evaluated according to:

- cycle time
- throughput
- quality
- reliability
- cost
- resource utilization
- decision quality
- exception rate
- automation effectiveness
- autonomy effectiveness
- resilience
- stakeholder outcome
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance shall be measured across the complete process rather than isolated activities.

---

## 19.14 Process Optimization

Processes shall be continuously optimized using:

- operational data
- performance information
- customer feedback
- governance evidence
- risk information
- AI insights
- agent insights
- architecture intelligence
- financial outcomes

Optimization may include:

- removing unnecessary steps
- simplifying workflows
- improving decision points
- reallocating work
- increasing automation
- increasing autonomy
- strengthening controls
- changing technology
- redesigning process stages

Optimization shall remain aligned with enterprise strategy and governance.

---

## 19.15 Process Evolution

Processes shall evolve in response to:

- strategic change
- stakeholder needs
- operational experience
- technology change
- AI evolution
- agent evolution
- regulation
- security threats
- risk changes
- enterprise learning

Material changes shall trigger appropriate:

- architecture review
- risk assessment
- policy review
- authority review
- security review
- assurance
- change governance

---

## 19.16 Process Lifecycle

The autonomous process lifecycle shall be:

```text
Process Identification

↓

Process Design

↓

Process Assessment

↓

Process Authorization

↓

Process Deployment

↓

Process Operation

↓

Process Monitoring

↓

Process Assurance

↓

Process Optimization

↓

Process Evolution

↓

Process Retirement
```

The lifecycle shall remain connected to capability, value stream, operating model, and Enterprise Architecture.

---

## 19.17 Process Performance and Maturity

The Enterprise Autonomous Process Operating Model Framework shall evaluate:

- process maturity
- process effectiveness
- process efficiency
- autonomy maturity
- process observability
- process governance
- process risk
- process resilience
- process adaptability
- process innovation
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance indicators shall continuously strengthen enterprise process management.

---

# 20. Enterprise Autonomous Decision Operating Framework

## 20.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Autonomous Decision Operating Framework establishes the canonical methodology for embedding governed decision-making directly into enterprise operating processes, capabilities, and value streams.

Decisions are the points at which enterprise information, policies, authority, risk, intelligence, and objectives are transformed into operational choices.

Within an Autonomous Enterprise, decision-making may involve humans, Artificial Intelligence, intelligent agents, automated decision engines, or combinations of these.

Enterprise Architects shall ensure that every material autonomous decision remains:

- purpose-aligned
- policy-constrained
- authority-aware
- risk-proportional
- observable
- explainable
- evidence-based
- accountable

The objective is:

> **To create a governed enterprise decision system capable of making high-quality decisions at the appropriate speed, scale, and level of autonomy.**

---

## 20.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Autonomous Decision Operating Framework shall:

- establish a common enterprise decision model
- connect decisions with enterprise objectives
- define decision ownership
- integrate human and machine intelligence
- improve decision quality
- improve decision speed
- strengthen decision governance
- improve decision traceability
- support bounded autonomy
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 20.3 Decision Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Enterprise Objective

↓

Decision Context

↓

Information

↓

Policy

↓

Risk

↓

Authority

↓

Intelligence

↓

Recommendation

↓

Decision

↓

Execution

↓

Outcome

↓

Evidence

↓

Learning
```

Every material decision shall be traceable to the context, information, authority, policies, risks, and outcomes associated with it.

---

## 20.4 Decision Domains

Enterprise Autonomous Decision Operating shall govern:

### Strategic Decisions

Decisions concerning:

- enterprise strategy
- transformation
- major investments
- organizational direction
- strategic partnerships
- enterprise architecture

---

### Tactical Decisions

Decisions concerning:

- portfolio management
- resource allocation
- capability development
- program priorities
- operational planning
- technology selection

---

### Operational Decisions

Decisions concerning:

- workflow execution
- resource allocation
- scheduling
- service management
- customer interaction
- operational optimization

---

### Autonomous Control Decisions

Decisions protecting:

- security
- continuity
- resilience
- compliance
- system integrity
- operational stability

---

### Exceptional Decisions

Decisions outside approved policies, authority, risk thresholds, or operating boundaries.

Exceptional decisions shall be escalated to an appropriately authorized human or governance authority.

---

## 20.5 Decision Ownership

Every material decision shall have:

- decision owner
- decision authority
- decision purpose
- decision scope
- decision criteria
- information requirements
- policy requirements
- risk requirements
- escalation authority
- evidence requirements

Decision ownership shall remain traceable even when the decision is executed autonomously.

---

## 20.6 Decision Operating Modes

Decisions may operate through:

### Human Decision

The human analyzes and decides.

### AI-Assisted Decision

AI provides analysis or recommendation while the human decides.

### AI-Recommended Decision

AI produces a formal recommendation requiring human approval.

### Human-Supervised Autonomous Decision

The autonomous capability decides within approved boundaries while humans supervise.

### Bounded Autonomous Decision

The autonomous capability independently decides and executes within defined policy, authority, and risk boundaries.

### Adaptive Autonomous Decision

The autonomous capability adapts its decision behavior within approved governance constraints based on validated learning and changing context.

---

## 20.7 Decision Quality

Decision quality shall be evaluated using:

- accuracy
- relevance
- timeliness
- consistency
- explainability
- confidence
- policy compliance
- risk alignment
- outcome quality
- stakeholder impact

Decision quality shall be assessed using outcomes rather than recommendation quality alone.

---

## 20.8 Decision Context

Decision context shall include, where relevant:

- enterprise objective
- business conditions
- operational state
- stakeholder context
- financial context
- risk context
- security context
- regulatory context
- environmental context
- historical information
- current telemetry
- applicable policy
- applicable authority

Decision context shall remain traceable.

---

## 20.9 Decision Escalation

Decision escalation shall occur when:

- authority is insufficient
- risk exceeds thresholds
- confidence is insufficient
- information is inadequate
- policy conflicts exist
- consequences exceed approved limits
- uncertainty becomes material
- security conditions change
- abnormal behavior is detected

The escalation model is:

```text
Decision Detection

↓

Context Assessment

↓

Authority Check

↓

Risk Assessment

↓

Escalation

↓

Authorized Decision

↓

Execution

↓

Evidence
```

---

## 20.10 Decision Override

The enterprise shall maintain the ability to:

- reject recommendations
- override decisions
- cancel execution
- suspend decision capabilities
- revoke authority
- isolate affected services
- initiate emergency intervention

Override mechanisms shall remain operationally effective and tested.

---

## 20.11 Decision Evidence

Material decisions shall generate evidence containing, where appropriate:

- decision identity
- decision owner
- decision authority
- decision context
- information used
- policy applied
- risk conditions
- AI model
- agent
- recommendation
- decision
- action
- outcome
- human intervention

Decision evidence shall support:

- audit
- compliance
- accountability
- incident investigation
- assurance
- architecture review
- continuous learning

---

## 20.12 Decision Learning

Decision outcomes shall be used to improve:

- decision policies
- decision criteria
- models
- agents
- authority boundaries
- escalation thresholds
- operating processes
- enterprise architecture

The decision learning cycle is:

```text
Decision

↓

Outcome

↓

Evaluation

↓

Feedback

↓

Learning

↓

Improvement

↓

Governance Review

↓

Decision Evolution
```

Learning shall remain governed and shall not independently create new authority.

---

## 20.13 Decision Resilience

Critical decision capabilities shall support:

- alternative decision paths
- human fallback
- degraded operation
- decision suspension
- information fallback
- model fallback
- agent fallback
- manual execution
- recovery

The enterprise shall identify decisions where failure could materially affect enterprise purpose, strategic objectives, safety, security, or resilience.

---

## 20.14 Decision Performance and Maturity

The Enterprise Autonomous Decision Operating Framework shall evaluate:

- decision maturity
- decision quality
- decision speed
- decision consistency
- autonomy maturity
- escalation effectiveness
- override effectiveness
- decision resilience
- explainability
- stakeholder confidence
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance indicators shall continuously strengthen the enterprise decision system.

---

## Implementation Characteristics

The Enterprise Autonomous Process Operating Model Framework and the Enterprise Autonomous Decision Operating Framework shall remain:

- purpose-driven
- capability-aligned
- value-oriented
- governance-controlled
- policy-based
- authority-aware
- human-accountable
- risk-proportional
- intelligence-enabled
- evidence-driven
- observable
- explainable
- resilient
- measurable
- continuously evolving

These implementation characteristics establish the process and decision foundation of the Autonomous Enterprise, enabling enterprise processes and decisions to operate as governed, intelligent, resilient, measurable, and continuously improving components of the enterprise operating system.

---

**End of Part 2 – Section 3 of 8**

# EA-IMETA76

# Enterprise Architecture Autonomous Enterprise Governance & Operating Model

## Document Version 1.0

### Part 2 of 6

#### Section 4 of 8

---

# 21. Enterprise Autonomous Workforce Operating Model Framework

## 21.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Autonomous Workforce Operating Model Framework establishes the canonical methodology for designing, governing, organizing, operating, measuring, and continuously evolving the workforce of an Autonomous Enterprise.

The Autonomous Enterprise workforce shall no longer be understood exclusively as human employees.

It shall be understood as an integrated workforce consisting of:

```text
Human Workforce

+

Artificial Intelligence

+

Intelligent Agents

+

Automation

+

Digital Services

+

External Expertise

=

Integrated Enterprise Workforce
```

The objective is not to replace human capability indiscriminately.

The objective is:

> **To create the most effective combination of human expertise, artificial intelligence, intelligent agents, automation, and digital services for achieving enterprise outcomes while preserving accountability, governance, resilience, and human responsibility.**

Enterprise Architects shall therefore ensure that workforce architecture remains connected to:

- enterprise strategy
- enterprise capabilities
- value streams
- operating model
- governance
- authority
- skills
- information
- technology
- AI
- agents
- security
- risk
- enterprise outcomes

---

## 21.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Autonomous Workforce Operating Model Framework shall:

- establish a common autonomous workforce model
- connect workforce requirements with enterprise strategy
- define workforce responsibilities
- integrate human and digital workforce capabilities
- improve workforce productivity
- strengthen workforce governance
- improve workforce resilience
- enable continuous workforce development
- support controlled autonomy
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 21.3 Workforce Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Enterprise Strategy

↓

Enterprise Capabilities

↓

Value Streams

↓

Work Requirements

↓

Workforce Model

↓

Human + AI + Agents + Automation

↓

Roles & Responsibilities

↓

Skills & Knowledge

↓

Work Execution

↓

Performance

↓

Learning

↓

Workforce Evolution
```

Workforce architecture shall establish an explicit relationship between enterprise work and the workforce resources required to perform that work.

---

## 21.4 Workforce Domains

The Autonomous Enterprise workforce shall include:

### Human Workforce

Human employees, leaders, specialists, professionals, operators, managers, and subject-matter experts.

---

### Artificial Intelligence Workforce

AI capabilities providing:

- analysis
- prediction
- classification
- recommendation
- knowledge processing
- decision support
- content generation
- pattern recognition

---

### Intelligent Agent Workforce

Agents capable of:

- planning
- coordination
- execution
- monitoring
- interaction
- orchestration
- autonomous task completion

Agents shall operate only within approved authority and governance boundaries.

---

### Automation Workforce

Automated capabilities performing:

- deterministic tasks
- workflow execution
- system integration
- data processing
- routine operational activities

---

### Digital Service Workforce

Digital services providing:

- information
- transactions
- platforms
- APIs
- computational services
- enterprise services
- operational support

---

### External Workforce

External capabilities may include:

- consultants
- contractors
- suppliers
- partners
- specialist services
- professional advisors

External workforce participation shall remain subject to enterprise governance, security, contractual, and information requirements.

---

## 21.5 Workforce Responsibility Model

Every material work activity shall have explicit responsibility.

Responsibility shall identify:

- accountable owner
- work owner
- execution responsibility
- decision authority
- human responsibility
- AI responsibility where applicable
- agent responsibility where applicable
- control responsibility
- assurance responsibility
- escalation authority

The responsibility relationship is:

```text
Accountability

↓

Authority

↓

Responsibility

↓

Execution

↓

Evidence

↓

Outcome
```

Autonomous execution shall never eliminate accountability.

---

## 21.6 Workforce Allocation Model

Enterprise work shall be allocated according to:

- complexity
- risk
- consequence
- required judgment
- accountability
- reversibility
- speed
- scale
- cost
- enterprise value

Work may be allocated as:

### Human-Executed

Humans perform the activity directly.

### Human-Augmented

Technology and AI increase human capability while humans retain responsibility.

### AI-Assisted

AI supports analysis, recommendation, prediction, or decision support.

### Agent-Assisted

Agents perform defined activities under human or governance supervision.

### Agent-Executed

Agents execute defined activities within approved authority.

### Automated

Deterministic activities execute automatically.

### Autonomous

An intelligent capability independently performs approved work within defined governance boundaries.

---

## 21.7 Workforce Role Architecture

Roles within the Autonomous Enterprise shall be defined according to responsibilities rather than merely organizational positions.

Roles may include:

- strategic decision-maker
- enterprise architect
- capability owner
- process owner
- value stream owner
- AI owner
- agent owner
- information owner
- security owner
- risk owner
- governance owner
- human oversight authority
- operational owner
- assurance owner

One individual or organizational unit may hold multiple roles where appropriate, provided that conflicts of interest and segregation-of-duty requirements remain controlled.

---

## 21.8 Human Workforce Evolution

The increasing use of AI, agents, and automation shall change human work.

Enterprise workforce evolution shall include:

- reskilling
- upskilling
- role redesign
- new specialist roles
- AI literacy
- agent literacy
- governance literacy
- data literacy
- continuous learning
- knowledge transfer

The objective shall be to increase human capability rather than simply reduce human participation.

---

## 21.9 AI and Agent Workforce Governance

AI and agents shall be governed as enterprise workforce capabilities.

Governance shall include:

- identity
- ownership
- authority
- purpose
- permitted activities
- information access
- tool access
- decision rights
- performance
- risk
- security
- lifecycle
- retirement

AI and agents shall not be granted authority solely because they possess technical capability.

Technical capability and governance authority shall remain separate.

---

## 21.10 Workforce Capacity Management

Workforce capacity shall be managed across:

- human capacity
- AI capacity
- agent capacity
- automation capacity
- technology capacity
- external capacity

Capacity management shall consider:

- demand
- workload
- criticality
- availability
- resilience
- cost
- performance
- strategic importance

The enterprise shall maintain sufficient capacity to continue critical operations during disruption.

---

## 21.11 Workforce Performance

Workforce performance shall evaluate:

- work outcomes
- productivity
- quality
- reliability
- decision quality
- capacity utilization
- collaboration
- resilience
- innovation
- stakeholder outcomes
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance evaluation shall not be limited to activity volume.

Outcome and value shall remain primary measures.

---

## 21.12 Workforce Resilience

The Autonomous Enterprise workforce shall be designed for resilience.

Resilience shall include:

- skills redundancy
- role redundancy
- cross-training
- knowledge preservation
- AI fallback
- agent fallback
- human fallback
- alternative service providers
- continuity arrangements
- recovery procedures

Critical workforce dependencies shall be identified and managed.

---

## 21.13 Workforce Learning

Workforce learning shall include:

- human learning
- organizational learning
- AI learning
- agent learning
- process learning
- capability learning
- governance learning

Learning shall remain controlled and evidence-based.

AI and agents shall not independently alter material enterprise policies or authority structures unless explicitly authorized.

---

## 21.14 Workforce Evolution

Workforce architecture shall continuously evolve in response to:

- enterprise strategy
- technology change
- AI development
- agent development
- workforce demographics
- market conditions
- regulatory requirements
- security requirements
- enterprise performance
- stakeholder expectations

Material workforce changes shall trigger appropriate:

- architecture review
- governance review
- risk assessment
- security review
- organizational review
- capability review

---

## 21.15 Workforce Lifecycle

The autonomous workforce lifecycle shall be:

```text
Work Identification

↓

Workforce Requirement

↓

Workforce Design

↓

Workforce Allocation

↓

Authorization

↓

Deployment

↓

Operation

↓

Performance Monitoring

↓

Learning

↓

Optimization

↓

Evolution

↓

Retirement or Replacement
```

The lifecycle shall apply to human and digital workforce capabilities where appropriate.

---

## 21.16 Workforce Performance and Maturity

The Enterprise Autonomous Workforce Operating Model Framework shall evaluate:

- workforce maturity
- human capability
- AI capability
- agent capability
- workforce productivity
- workforce resilience
- workforce adaptability
- workforce governance
- workforce innovation
- workforce learning
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

Performance indicators shall continuously strengthen the enterprise workforce.

---

# 22. Enterprise Human–AI–Agent Collaboration Operating Framework

## 22.1 Purpose

The Enterprise Human–AI–Agent Collaboration Operating Framework establishes the canonical methodology for designing and governing collaboration between human workers, Artificial Intelligence, intelligent agents, automation, and digital services.

The framework ensures that the combined workforce operates as a coherent system rather than as disconnected technologies and organizational roles.

The collaboration model shall preserve:

- human accountability
- enterprise governance
- decision authority
- transparency
- security
- risk control
- operational resilience

while enabling AI and agents to increase enterprise speed, scale, intelligence, consistency, and adaptability.

---

## 22.2 Objectives

The Enterprise Human–AI–Agent Collaboration Operating Framework shall:

- establish human–AI–agent collaboration principles
- define collaboration responsibilities
- allocate work appropriately
- strengthen decision quality
- improve operational speed
- improve enterprise scalability
- preserve human accountability
- strengthen collaboration governance
- improve workforce resilience
- maximize Sustainable Enterprise Value

---

## 22.3 Collaboration Architecture

The recommended logical architecture consists of:

```text
Enterprise Objective

↓

Work Requirement

↓

Role & Responsibility

↓

Human Intelligence

+

AI Intelligence

+

Agent Execution

+

Automation

↓

Collaborative Decision

↓

Collaborative Execution

↓

Observation

↓

Outcome

↓

Feedback

↓

Learning
```

The collaboration architecture shall explicitly define the responsibilities of each participant.

---

## 22.4 Collaboration Roles

Human–AI–agent collaboration may include:

### Human

Provides:

- judgment
- accountability
- contextual understanding
- ethical reasoning
- strategic direction
- stakeholder engagement
- exception handling

---

### Artificial Intelligence

Provides:

- analysis
- prediction
- pattern recognition
- recommendation
- knowledge synthesis
- decision support
- content generation

---

### Intelligent Agent

Provides:

- planning
- coordination
- task execution
- monitoring
- orchestration
- interaction
- autonomous action within approved boundaries

---

### Automation

Provides:

- deterministic execution
- workflow processing
- integration
- repetitive task execution
- data processing

---

### Digital Services

Provide:

- information
- transactions
- computation
- communication
- enterprise services
- operational capabilities

---

## 22.5 Collaboration Patterns

The enterprise may use different collaboration patterns.

### Human-Led

The human leads and AI or agents provide support.

### AI-Assisted

AI provides intelligence while the human remains responsible.

### Agent-Assisted

Agents perform supporting tasks under human direction.

### Agent-Led with Human Supervision

The agent performs operational activities while humans supervise.

### Autonomous with Human Governance

The autonomous capability operates independently within approved boundaries while humans govern policy, authority, risk, performance, and exceptions.

### Multi-Agent Collaboration

Multiple agents collaborate to complete a complex enterprise activity.

Multi-agent collaboration shall include explicit:

- identity
- authority
- communication boundaries
- coordination rules
- conflict handling
- escalation
- evidence

---

## 22.6 Collaboration Authority

Collaboration authority shall define:

- who may initiate work
- who may approve work
- who may execute work
- who may override decisions
- who may suspend activity
- who may change authority
- who owns the outcome

AI and agents shall not obtain authority implicitly through collaboration.

---

## 22.7 Collaboration Decision Model

Collaborative decisions shall distinguish between:

```text
Information

↓

Analysis

↓

Recommendation

↓

Human / Governance Review

↓

Decision

↓

Execution

↓

Observation

↓

Outcome
```

The responsible actor for each stage shall be explicitly defined.

---

## 22.8 Collaboration Communication

Human–AI–agent communication shall support:

- clear intent
- context
- role identity
- authority
- task definition
- expected outcome
- constraints
- escalation
- evidence

Agent-to-agent communication shall remain subject to authentication, authorization, monitoring, and governance.

---

## 22.9 Collaboration Conflict Management

Conflicts may occur between:

- human decisions
- AI recommendations
- agent actions
- enterprise policies
- operational conditions
- risk requirements

Conflict management shall follow:

```text
Conflict Detection

↓

Context Assessment

↓

Authority Check

↓

Policy Check

↓

Risk Assessment

↓

Resolution

↓

Escalation if Required

↓

Evidence

↓

Learning
```

Human or governance authority shall prevail where the conflict exceeds autonomous authority.

---

## 22.10 Collaboration Trust

Trust shall be based on:

- identity
- authority
- transparency
- evidence
- performance
- reliability
- explainability
- security
- policy compliance
- predictable behavior

Trust shall not be based solely on historical performance.

Autonomous capabilities shall remain continuously observable and governable.

---

## 22.11 Collaboration Safety and Resilience

Human–AI–agent collaboration shall support:

- safe failure
- human fallback
- agent fallback
- service fallback
- controlled shutdown
- isolation
- recovery
- continuity
- incident response

Critical collaboration patterns shall be tested under degraded and failure conditions.

---

## 22.12 Collaboration Learning

Collaboration outcomes shall improve:

- work allocation
- role design
- decision models
- AI models
- agent behavior
- process design
- governance
- workforce skills

Learning shall remain subject to enterprise governance.

---

## 22.13 Collaboration Performance

The Enterprise Human–AI–Agent Collaboration Operating Framework shall evaluate:

- collaboration effectiveness
- decision quality
- work allocation effectiveness
- productivity
- response time
- human satisfaction
- AI usefulness
- agent effectiveness
- collaboration resilience
- governance effectiveness
- stakeholder outcomes
- Sustainable Enterprise Value realization

---

## 22.14 Collaboration Maturity

Collaboration maturity shall progress from:

```text
Human-Only

↓

Human + Automation

↓

Human + AI Assistance

↓

Human + Agents

↓

Human–AI–Agent Collaboration

↓

Governed Autonomous Collaboration

↓

Adaptive Human–AI–Agent Enterprise Workforce
```

The enterprise shall increase collaboration autonomy only when governance, risk, security, observability, and human oversight are sufficiently mature.

---

## Implementation Characteristics

The Enterprise Autonomous Workforce Operating Model Framework and the Enterprise Human–AI–Agent Collaboration Operating Framework shall remain:

- purpose-driven
- capability-aligned
- value-oriented
- human-accountable
- governance-controlled
- authority-aware
- risk-proportional
- intelligence-enabled
- evidence-driven
- secure
- observable
- resilient
- measurable
- continuously learning
- continuously evolving

These implementation characteristics establish the workforce and human–AI–agent collaboration foundation of the Autonomous Enterprise, enabling human expertise, artificial intelligence, intelligent agents, automation, and digital services to operate as an integrated, governed, resilient, and continuously improving enterprise workforce.

---

**End of Part 2 – Section 4 of 8**

# EA-IMETA76

# Enterprise Architecture Autonomous Enterprise Governance & Operating Model

## Document Version 1.0
